mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over a three-month window indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months during a period of stable unemployment signals accelerated labor absorption without wage inflation, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for three consecutive months and UNRATE stable
regime_hint: tight labor market with stable unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for six consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing activity, which raises input utilization and profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 50% of triggered episodes across all regimes.
